page: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The configuration delivers 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 81,317.48 and a Passmark CPU score of 55,855.44. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 4,502.42 GB/sec and uncached large-block write speeds at 97.63 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and gzip single-threaded compression falling into the bottom 25% of benchmarks. LLM text generation is also limited, with the medium 7B model achieving only 5.69 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5b.24xlarge provides high resource density for memory-bound applications, trading off local storage and high single-thread speeds for massive memory capacity and parallel processing power. It is highly optimized for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and high-throughput caching. Benchmark results confirm its strength in database operations, scoring 21,639.75 on Passmark, and Redis SET operations, which reach 74.14 million operations per second. This makes the instance suitable for large relational databases, in-memory data stores, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz. It includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The instance delivers strong multi-core performance, outstanding memory bandwidth, and high database throughput, as demonstrated by 74.14 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds are relatively weak. Qualitatively, the instance offers high memory density, making it a cost-effective choice for large-scale in-memory databases and caching layers rather than compute-bound or single-threaded tasks. It is best suited for enterprise database operations, in-memory data stores, and high-throughput web serving.
